analysis:
This PR changes developer documentation only (docs/developer/build.md and docs/developer/test.md). It touches no provider code, no wire protocol and no key or attestation paths. TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009 and TB-011, and assets A-001 to A-017, are not affected by any supplied change.

The one supply-chain-relevant addition is build.md lines 77-88. It describes scripts/fetch-metallib.sh using a local metal-cpp archive. The archive is either the sandbox-runner image copy at /usr/local/libexec/darkbloom/share/metal-cpp/metal-cpp_26.zip or one named by MLX_METAL_CPP_ARCHIVE. It is used only when its SHA-256 matches the script's pin, otherwise FetchContent downloads it as before. The documented behavior therefore preserves integrity verification and cache-key identity, and adds no new trust assumption. I could not check the script itself, so whether it actually enforces the pinned hash before unzipping is an unverified contract. A later pass should confirm that, and that a mismatch falls back rather than being skipped.

The other build.md edits describe CI structure: build-once jobs, the ci-tested-tree skip record, routing and size grants, cache scopes, and the save-caches rule. Caches are saved only on master and dev pushes, and checkouts use persist-credentials: false. The docs say records count only from successful, same-repository, same-workflow runs. Release and signing keep literal Blacksmith labels, and master's CI restores only the strict cache tier. These are described as controls and are not weakened. They are outside the provider threat model's scope, and I could not verify the workflows themselves.

I saw only the metadata for test.md (unit 67373c0eff1153bd:0), with no text. Its patch excerpt shows test-sharding and CI wording changes only. No threat-model update is needed.
